title: sessionConversation
description: A code session read as TALK, of any provider: the conversation projection of a converted session (session.json), written beside it as conversation.json by its provider's project_conversation.py. What projects is each provider's own rule, stated in that script; claude's: only user and assistant records project — no sidechain records (a subagent's transcript is its own session), no meta records, no tool-result carrier records (a user record with toolUseResult is the harness returning a tool's output, not the user speaking) — and each turn is the record's visible text: text blocks joined, while thinking, tool_use and tool_result blocks are working, not talk, and remain in session.json. A record whose projection is empty (a pure tool step) contributes no turn, so messages may legitimately be empty for a session that is all tool work. Roles use the corpus vocabulary ('human'/'assistant', as in chat-capture/markdownConversation), because this shape is the projection source for the session corpus render under data/output/markdown/<provider>/code/conversations/. See model_join.csv for field correspondences with the session and markdownConversation families.

SessionConversation.title: SessionConversation
SessionConversation.description: One session reduced to its conversation: identity, span, title dressing, and the ordered role-tagged turns.

provider.description: The provider whose harness recorded the session, a row of rsc/provider/providers.csv - the segment of the store, the cache and the corpus root the session sits under.

harness.description: The harness that recorded the session, as its provider names it - the corpus preamble's dressing.

title.description: The session's title as its harness gives one — claude: the LAST ai-title record's aiTitle, the same dressing authority agent.py's census uses; gemini: the summary row's title; '' where the session never received one (every observed local session is titled; the empty case is reachable by construction).

project.description: The project directory name the session belongs to — the harness's lossy cwd encoding (/ replaced by -).

session_id.description: The session's uuid — the name its harness stores it under (claude: the .jsonl stem; gemini: the session directory), the session's identity everywhere (tmp/cache/ dirs, transported copies, corpus frontmatter).

created.description: The earliest record timestamp in the WHOLE session (ISO 8601, Z, to the precision the harness records: claude milliseconds, gemini seconds) — the session's span, not the projected turns': ordering authority for corpus ordinals.

last_activity.description: The latest record timestamp in the WHOLE session (ISO 8601, Z, to the harness's precision) — a session that ends in tool work still ends then.

messages.description: The conversation turns in record order. May be empty: a session that is all tool work projects no talk.

UuidV4.title: UuidV4
UuidV4.description: Standard UUID version 4 (randomly generated). Pattern: xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx where y is 8, 9, a, or b.

Message.title: Message
Message.description: One projected turn: the source record's uuid (the turn's durable identity — rendered as an HTML anchor on the corpus heading, exactly as markdownConversation turns are), its role, its timestamp, and its visible text.

uuid.description: The source user/assistant record's uuid — addresses the turn durably across corpus renumberings. Absent where the provider's record carries no identity of its own (a gemini step): the corpus then anchors the turn by role and count.

role.description: The corpus role vocabulary: a user record projects as 'human' (matching markdownConversation), an assistant record as 'assistant'.

timestamp.description: The source record's timestamp (ISO 8601, Z, to the harness's precision).

content.description: The turn's visible text: a bare string content verbatim, else the record's text blocks joined by blank lines. Never empty — an empty projection contributes no turn at all.
